subject: PrismBank: prioritization request for routing + residency features
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: PrismBank: prioritization request for routing + residency features

Laura / team —

Quick context: PrismBank is targeting a July production cutover for a customer-facing payments assistant. They signed a letter of intent and procurement expects a short pilot to go live week of 7/19. The deal is contingent on two items they listed in the mutual action plan: (1) an enterprise-grade failover policy that guarantees no visible errors during model routing incidents (they prefer regional fallthrough to a carve-out model), and (2) a lightweight residency hint so the customer can request session affinity for bursts tied to a region/tenant for the first 30–60 seconds.

Why this is urgent: procurement is pushing for a verify-by-date and Prism is evaluating other vendors if we can't commit to a short roadmap. The approximated ARR for the first 12 months is $380k; long-term opportunity through cross-sell is material.

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate whether we can (A) ship an MVP routing shim + residency hint API within ~2 weeks for pilot use, and (B) a more durable pinning solution within ~6 weeks after pilot? If we can’t meet (A), we risk losing the pilot.

Attached: Prism_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.pdf (procurement milestones).

Next steps I need from you by EOD Thu: a recommended scoping (MVP vs full), estimated engineering effort, and any obvious blocking security/compliance asks. I can surface a hard deadline from the customer if helpful.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrismBank: prioritization request for routing + residency features

Thanks — this is clear and appreciated.

High-level reaction: Product agrees the pilot needs a narrow, well-scoped MVP to keep risk low. Proposed split:
- MVP (target ~2 weeks): a routing "shim" (policy layer) that supports failover to a selectable fallback model/region + a residency-hint API (stateless header) that signals the routing layer to bias affinity for a short window. No durable KV pinning, no cross-tenant cache guarantees.
- Phase 2 (target ~6 weeks post-MVP): engineering work to add durable session pinning, eviction policies, and end-to-end SLO verification with Canary.

Questions for dev: what are the engineering risks for the shim + hint API? Are there any infra or security gating items (e.g., KMS/keys, traffic isolation concerns) that will block a 2-week delivery?

If Dev thinks 2 weeks is unrealistic, please propose the minimum viable cut that removes the customer blocker.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrismBank: prioritization request for routing + residency features

Laura —

Thanks for the proposed split. Technical perspective and trade-offs below.

Summary: I think an MVP routing shim + residency-hint header is feasible on an accelerated path, but "2 weeks" is tight if we include QA, load testing, and a minimal canary. My recommended delivery plan is a 10-business-day sprint for the shim + hint API if we take the following scope decisions:
- No persistent session pinning in MVP. The shim maintains short-lived in-memory affinity (per-runtime) and relies on prefix caching for warm KV entries. This reduces complexity but means affinity isn’t globally consistent across pods.
- Routing policy will accept a header X-Residency-Hint: {region}:{session-id} and bias placement; fallback rules: same-region fallback -> cross-region fallback -> default model.
- Instrumentation/tracing hooks added to verify failover in canary.

Effort estimate (rough):
- Routing shim + policy engine: 5 dev days (1.5 FTE)
- Residency hint parser + lightweight in-memory affinity: 3 dev days
- Tests (unit + integration) + canary infra + observability dashboards: 2 dev days
Total: ~10 dev-days (can parallelize across two engineers for ~7 calendar days).

Risks / blockers:
- Global affinity: without a global store (Redis/consensus), sessions could be served by different pods and lose affinity on failover — acceptable for pilot but note this to the customer.
- Security: need a short review on headers and auth propagation; procurement may want explicit logging retention artifacts. Grace, can you confirm if the customer needs logs retained for audit and the timeframe?

Quick workaround for a 2-week calendar target: we can ship a config-guarded shim that runs in front of a canary pool and document the limitations. That path saves ~2 calendar days versus fully instrumented canary.

I attached a short spec with API shapes and diagrams: redwood-routing-residency-spec.md.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Engineering Lead, Runtime

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrismBank: prioritization request for routing + residency features

Appreciate the quick estimate, Dev — that helps a lot.

Decision: Product and Sales align on the MVP compromise: routing shim + residency-hint header with the "in-memory per-runtime affinity" approach. We will ship the shim behind a config flag and run it in a canary pool for the pilot.

Action items for this thread:
- Dev: please open a tracking ticket and PR with the API contract + release checklist. Target minimal canary in 10 dev-days; if you can shave to 7 calendar days, call it out.
- Grace: confirm audit/log retention ask from PrismBank (they mentioned SOC 2-ish audit evidence in the mutual action plan).
- Camila: I'll update the mutual action plan to reflect the reduced-scope MVP and a Phase 2 timeline. I will also send PrismBank the revised milestones once we have a ticket/ETA.

Forwarding to PrismBank procurement for transparency — Kate, procurement team, below is our internal alignment and a short note on next steps.

--Forwarded message--
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Liu <kate.liu@prismbank.com>; procurement@prismbank.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood: proposed pilot scope & next steps (routing + residency)

Kate —

Thanks for the call today. Internal update: we will deliver an MVP routing shim + residency-hint API for pilot, with a Phase 2 durable pinning plan thereafter. We expect to have an ETA within 48 business hours once Eng opens the tracking ticket.

Ask from you: please confirm that PrismBank is comfortable proceeding with the MVP constraints (per-runtime affinity, documented limitations on global session guarantees) and that procurement is OK with a pilot acceptance criteria that focuses on availability and no visible user errors during failover.

I will share the revised mutual action plan after we have the ticket/ETA.

Best —
Dylan

From: Kate Liu <kate.liu@prismbank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood: proposed pilot scope & next steps (routing + residency)

Dylan —

Thanks for the update and for being explicit about limitations. Procurement and engineering here have talked it over: PrismBank is willing to proceed with the MVP constraints for pilot provided we get the following in writing:
1) A documented list of expected behaviors during failover (what the user will see).
2) A timeline to Phase 2 with commitment to durable pinning and audit evidence for sessions.
3) A runbook for diagnosing failover incidents during pilot.

If you can provide the above items and the Eng ETA in the next 48 hours, procurement will confirm the pilot milestone and we can proceed with PO paperwork.

—Kate Liu
Head of Platform Integrations, PrismBank
